title: Unowned File Detection
exclusions: Detects only directory entries on explicitly configured Linux scan roots whose inode `st_uid` has no user record, whose `st_gid` has no group record, or both, through the scanning host's effective Name Service Switch (NSS) configuration at scan time. It does not mean the inode lacks numeric ownership, that its owner is disabled, expired, locked, absent from `/etc/passwd`, unauthorized for the path, or unable to access the file; ACLs, capabilities, labels, namespaces, and application ownership policy are separate controls. The default `find -P ... -xdev` contract does not follow symbolic links and does not descend onto a different `st_dev`; every separate filesystem must be named as its own root. Unlisted local, removable, network, container-overlay, pseudo, transient, and offline filesystems are out of scope. `-xdev` is a device boundary, not a universal mount boundary: a same-device bind mount can remain traversable and must be removed from policy or handled as an approved duplicate path. Unreadable directories, nonzero `find` exits, failed NSS sentinels, changed NSS answers, malformed/duplicate events, incomplete manifests, and silent hosts are collection defects, never healthy zero findings. Files created or deleted during traversal can escape or vanish from one point-in-time scan. This UC does not reconstruct historical account ownership, inspect file contents, detect every malicious ownership change, remediate with `chown`, prove compromise, or establish regulatory compliance.
evidence: When deployed, retain the version-controlled collector and SHA-256, exact GNU find and Python/glibc versions, effective `passwd:` and `group:` NSS configuration, configured user/group sentinel mappings, approved scan-root inventory with filesystem type/device and explicit omissions, service/timer and Universal Forwarder monitor/props stanzas, and `linux_unowned_file_detection` saved-search definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, and alert records. For each scan preserve its single manifest, scan ID/times, root/completion/failure counts, finding and race/error counts, collector status, find exits, and all associated finding events with exact base64 path, display path, path hash, scan root, device/inode, type/mode, UID/GID, resolution flags/names, timestamps, exception decision, owner/ticket, and analyst disposition. Keep positive, negative, NSS-failure, mount-boundary, malformed-batch, and exception-expiry test outputs. These artifacts demonstrate what the configured host NSS and completed bounded traversal reported; they do not prove historical ownership, content integrity, continuous coverage, or malicious causation.

controlTest.positiveScenario: On an isolated disposable Linux filesystem, first prove `getent passwd 61001` and `getent group 61002` return no record while configured local and remote NSS sentinels resolve in both name-to-ID and ID-to-name directions. Create `/mnt/uc112/both-unowned`, set numeric ownership to `61001:61002`, and create a `root:root` control file. Run the supplied collector with `/mnt/uc112` as its only root. Expect one `ownership_finding` plus one `collector_status=complete` manifest with `root_count=1`, `completed_root_count=1`, `failed_root_count=0`, `finding_count=1`, and zero stat/resolution-change errors. Run the saved search against that isolated scan. Expect exactly one high-severity row for the test path with `uid=61001`, `gid=61002`, `is_unowned_user=1`, `is_unowned_group=1`, `issue_type=user_and_group_unowned`, and the manifest's scan ID; the root-owned control file must not appear. Restore or delete the test inode after evidence capture.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Exercise four independent fail-closed controls. (1) Scan only resolved `root:root` files and expect a complete zero-finding manifest and zero detection rows. (2) Mount a separate test filesystem below the configured root and place an unowned file there; with only the parent root configured, `-xdev` must omit the child file, then adding the child mount as a separate root must produce exactly one row. Do not use a same-device bind mount for this test. (3) Break one configured remote NSS sentinel or inject a manifest with `collector_status=degraded`, a nonzero failed-root/stat/resolution-change count, a duplicate manifest, or a declared-versus-observed finding mismatch; the primary detection must return zero rows and the separate collector-health alert must fire. (4) Add an exact, approved `host,path_hash,issue_type` exception with a bounded active UTC interval to the positive fixture and expect zero notified rows; expire it and expect the original row to return. No variant may treat a failed or absent scan as a clean ownership result.

dataSources: Primary source: one newline-delimited JSON batch per scheduled host scan, written by the supplied deployment-owned collector and monitored into the deployment-selected `index=os` as `source=linux_unowned_files sourcetype=linux:unowned_files`. The collector requires GNU find and runs `find -P <root> -xdev \( -nouser -o -nogroup \) -print0` separately for every approved root. GNU/POSIX define `-nouser` and `-nogroup` by failure to map the file's numeric owner IDs; the collector then re-reads the inode with `lstat`, whose `st_uid` and `st_gid` remain the authoritative numeric owners, and repeats user/group NSS resolution before emitting a finding. Name-to-ID and ID-to-name sentinels are checked before and after traversal so a directory-service failure cannot silently become a mass finding. Each finding supplies `event_time`, `schema_version`, `record_type`, `scan_id`, `scan_started_epoch`, `scan_root`, `path`, `path_b64`, `path_hash`, `device_id`, `inode`, `file_type`, `mode_octal`, `size_bytes`, `mtime_epoch`, `ctime_epoch`, `uid`, `gid`, `is_unowned_user`, `is_unowned_group`, `user_name`, and `group_name`. The terminal manifest supplies completion and error counts. One complete scan emits one event per unresolved path plus exactly one manifest; a clean host emits only the manifest. Index, source, and source type are local contracts, not vendor-provided fields.
app: A deployment-owned app such as `TA_linux_unowned_files` provides the `linux:unowned_files` JSON source type, file-monitor input, saved search, lookup definition, dashboard, and permissions. Run the collector under a separately controlled operating-system service identity with enough directory traversal permission; do not make the Universal Forwarder root merely to scan files. The forwarder monitors only the root-owned, append-only NDJSON output. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) can provide adjacent Unix account or filesystem context, but its documented source types do not provide this complete-scan ownership contract. No premium Splunk app is required.
spl:
index=os source=linux_unowned_files sourcetype="linux:unowned_files" schema_version=1 earliest=-30h@h latest=-10m@m
| eval scan_started_epoch=tonumber(scan_started_epoch), uid=tonumber(uid), gid=tonumber(gid), is_unowned_user=tonumber(is_unowned_user), is_unowned_group=tonumber(is_unowned_group), root_count=tonumber(root_count), completed_root_count=tonumber(completed_root_count), failed_root_count=tonumber(failed_root_count), finding_count=tonumber(finding_count), stat_error_count=tonumber(stat_error_count), resolution_changed_count=tonumber(resolution_changed_count)
| eventstats max(eval(if(record_type="manifest",scan_started_epoch,null()))) AS latest_scan_started_epoch BY host
| where scan_started_epoch=latest_scan_started_epoch
| eventstats count(eval(record_type="manifest")) AS manifest_events count(eval(record_type="ownership_finding")) AS observed_finding_count values(eval(if(record_type="manifest",collector_status,null()))) AS manifest_statuses max(eval(if(record_type="manifest",finding_count,null()))) AS declared_finding_count max(eval(if(record_type="manifest",root_count,null()))) AS declared_root_count max(eval(if(record_type="manifest",completed_root_count,null()))) AS completed_roots max(eval(if(record_type="manifest",failed_root_count,null()))) AS failed_roots max(eval(if(record_type="manifest",stat_error_count,null()))) AS scan_stat_errors max(eval(if(record_type="manifest",resolution_changed_count,null()))) AS scan_resolution_changes BY host scan_id
| eval manifest_status=if(mvcount(manifest_statuses)=1,mvindex(manifest_statuses,0),null())
| where record_type="ownership_finding" AND manifest_events=1 AND manifest_status="complete" AND declared_root_count>0 AND completed_roots=declared_root_count AND failed_roots=0 AND scan_stat_errors=0 AND scan_resolution_changes=0 AND observed_finding_count=declared_finding_count
| where uid>=0 AND gid>=0 AND in(is_unowned_user,0,1) AND in(is_unowned_group,0,1) AND (is_unowned_user=1 OR is_unowned_group=1) AND len(path_hash)=64 AND len(path)>0 AND len(scan_root)>0
| eval issue_type=case(is_unowned_user=1 AND is_unowned_group=1,"user_and_group_unowned",is_unowned_user=1,"user_unowned",is_unowned_group=1,"group_unowned"), severity=if(is_unowned_user=1,"high","medium"), use_case="UC-1.1.112"
| lookup linux_unowned_file_exceptions.csv host path_hash issue_type OUTPUT valid_from_epoch valid_until_epoch exception_reason exception_owner exception_ticket
| eval valid_from_epoch=tonumber(valid_from_epoch), valid_until_epoch=tonumber(valid_until_epoch), exception_active=if(valid_from_epoch<=now() AND now()<valid_until_epoch AND len(exception_reason)>0 AND len(exception_owner)>0 AND len(exception_ticket)>0,1,0)
| where exception_active!=1
| eval interpretation="The inode's numeric UID or GID did not resolve through this host's effective NSS during a manifest-complete scan. Confirm NSS health, account lifecycle, namespace and restore context before changing ownership."
| table severity host issue_type path path_hash scan_root file_type mode_octal uid gid user_name group_name size_bytes mtime_epoch ctime_epoch device_id inode scan_id scan_started_epoch interpretation
| sort 0 severity host path
description: Identifies each path in the latest manifest-complete host scan whose inode numeric user ID, numeric group ID, or both have no corresponding record through that host's effective NSS. Each row retains exact scan, filesystem, inode, ownership, path, and resolution context; incomplete traversal and unstable NSS are rejected rather than interpreted as clean or unowned state.
value: Deleted accounts, incomplete restores, image migrations, package removal, UID/GID allocation drift, and namespace mistakes can leave files without a currently accountable principal, complicating patching, backup, incident response, and service recovery. A fail-closed inventory lets platform and security owners repair ownership deliberately while avoiding the dangerous mass-`chown` response that an LDAP/SSSD outage or an intentionally unmapped container ID could otherwise provoke.
implementation: Define an approved one-filesystem-per-root scan policy and representative local/remote NSS sentinels; deploy the supplied read-only GNU find/Python collector as an isolated operating-system service; and monitor its NDJSON output through a managed Universal Forwarder app as `linux:unowned_files`. Validate complete manifests, exact UID/GID and path fields, NSS failure behavior, and mount boundaries before saving the SPL as `linux_unowned_file_detection`. Run after each daily scan with ingestion delay, alert on returned file rows, and operate expected-host/manifest freshness separately. Investigate account, restore, namespace, package, and directory-service context before any owner change.
visualization: Use a latest-complete-scan findings table with severity, host, issue type, display path, scan root, file type/mode, numeric UID/GID, whichever owner name still resolves, device/inode, age, scan ID, and exception state. Add counts by host, scan root, issue type, numeric UID, numeric GID, file type, and age band; a host-by-day trend of complete-scan finding counts; and drilldowns to raw path base64 and inode metadata. Beside findings, show expected-host manifest freshness, scan duration, configured/completed/failed roots, NSS/collector status, vanished/stat/resolution-change/duplicate counts, and find version. Never chart absence of a manifest as zero unowned files, and never label a numeric unmapped container ID as malicious without namespace context.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable. Standard CIM datasets do not preserve a host traversal transaction, configured mount roots, complete-scan manifest, inode device/number, exact byte path, numeric ownership, current NSS resolution result, or collector error/race counters. A summary index may retain daily trends only after raw manifest/finding integrity has been evaluated; it must not replace source events needed to prove which scan and NSS state produced a finding.

knownFalsePositives:
A returned row means an inode's numeric UID or GID did not map through the host's effective NSS during a completed scan. That is an ownership-accountability finding, but it is not automatically corruption or compromise.

1. **Intentional container, user-namespace, rootless-runtime, or subordinate-ID ownership** — Host-visible numeric IDs may be valid only inside a user namespace or under `/etc/subuid` and `/etc/subgid`; the host NSS is not expected to resolve every mapped ID. Confirm the container/pod, namespace map, storage driver, workload owner, and path lifecycle. Prefer excluding the exact approved mount root from this host-level control or use a bounded exact path-hash exception; never create host accounts merely to silence namespace-owned storage.

2. **Restore, image import, shared disk, or cross-environment UID/GID mismatch** — Backups and machine images preserve numeric IDs that may belong to principals in the source estate. Confirm restore manifest, source identity registry, destination service account policy, and application test. Assign the destination owner through change control; do not infer a name from the same number on another host.

3. **Account or package removal before file cleanup** — Deliberate decommissioning can leave spool, cache, home, package, or service data briefly unmapped. Correlate package-manager and IAM tickets, path purpose, deletion/retention plan, and maintenance window. Suppress only the exact file/reason for a bounded cleanup period, then verify deletion or approved reassignment.

4. **Directory-service, SSSD, LDAP, NIS, winbind, or NSS module degradation** — A lookup outage can make many legitimate remote owners appear absent. Required local and remote name/ID sentinels before and after the scan are the principal safeguard. If counts jump across many unrelated UIDs/GIDs, check NSS configuration, cache/daemon health, DNS, TLS, network, backend latency, and `getent` in both directions. Treat any sentinel failure or changing answer as collector failure; never mass-`chown` during identity-service uncertainty.

5. **Cluster or shared-filesystem node has a different identity view** — NFS and clustered storage can present numeric ownership to clients whose NSS domains differ. This UC excludes such mounts unless explicitly approved. If included, scan from a designated node with the authoritative identity domain and record mount options, ID mapping, server/client ownership semantics, and failover behavior.

6. **Installer, extraction, build, or migration creates temporary numeric ownership** — Packaging tools, tar archives, CI builds, and data migrations can expose short-lived unmapped inodes. Match exact process/job, source archive, path, and bounded window. Persistent findings after job completion require cleanup; a schedule alone is not sufficient suppression.

7. **Filesystem races and path aliases** — A candidate can disappear between GNU find and `lstat`; the collector counts this as `vanished_path_count` and waits for the next scan. Same-device bind mounts can expose one inode under multiple paths because `-xdev` tests device ID, while hard links legitimately provide multiple directory entries. Review root policy and path/device/inode context. Do not deduplicate different paths solely by inode when each path has distinct operational ownership.

8. **Deliberately reserved or application-private numeric IDs** — Appliances, offline chroots, extracted root filesystems, and vendor software may reserve IDs without publishing them through host NSS. Require vendor or platform-owner documentation tying exact IDs and paths to a lifecycle. Keep those trees outside the host scan or use exact reviewed exceptions; broad UID-only exceptions can conceal unrelated files.

**Safe notification suppression:** use `linux_unowned_file_exceptions.csv` with headers `host,path_hash,issue_type,valid_from_epoch,valid_until_epoch,exception_reason,exception_owner,exception_ticket`. Match exact host, the collector's SHA-256 over exact path bytes, and one of `user_unowned`, `group_unowned`, or `user_and_group_unowned`; require numeric bounded UTC epochs, owner, reason, and ticket. Reject wildcard hosts/hashes, UID/GID-only fleet exceptions, open-ended windows, and any mechanism that suppresses missing manifests, failed roots, NSS sentinel failure, stat errors, resolution changes, malformed batches, or collector-health alerts.
mitreAttack: N/A (an unresolved numeric file owner is configuration/inventory evidence and does not by itself establish adversary behavior)
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against primary POSIX/GNU find, Linux stat, glibc UID/GID and NSS, and Splunk file-monitor, JSON, eventstats, lookup, and Unix add-on source-type documentation; only isolated collector syntax/smoke checks were performed, while filesystem/NSS estate behavior, SPL, fixtures, exception logic, performance, and production coverage were not runtime-tested; no Linux, identity, Splunk, security, production, or SME sign-off

cost.search_load_notes: One manifest plus one event per finding per host per daily scan produces low Splunk search volume; the dominant cost is host-side filesystem metadata traversal, which must be measured by filesystem class and is not represented by Splunk search load.
sources: host NSS passwd and group resolution

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and exact ownership definition

Assign a Linux platform owner, identity/NSS owner, filesystem owner, Splunk collection owner, and responder. Qualify the exact distribution's GNU find, Python 3 runtime linked to the host's effective libc/NSS stack, service manager, and Universal Forwarder. The search role needs read access to the selected OS index, the exception lookup, and permission to schedule a search. The collector identity needs read and execute/traverse permission across every in-scope tree; because broad traversal commonly requires privilege, run it as a narrowly managed operating-system service and monitor its output as the ordinary forwarder identity. Do not run the entire Universal Forwarder as root and do not grant the Splunk account unrestricted sudo.

The filesystem stores numeric ownership. Linux `stat` exposes `st_uid` as the user ID of the owner and `st_gid` as the group-owner ID. A file is **user-unowned for this control** only when the effective user database cannot return a record for that numeric UID at scan time; it is **group-unowned** only when the effective group database cannot return a record for that numeric GID. The Open Group defines `find -nouser` and `-nogroup` in those same `getpwuid`/`getgrgid` terms. The numeric fields never become blank. Root ownership, a locked or expired account, a missing local `/etc/passwd` line that resolves through LDAP, an ACL principal, or an unexpected-but-resolvable owner is not an unowned finding.

NSS makes the result contextual. `/etc/nsswitch.conf` defines source order and result actions separately for `passwd` and `group`; sources may include local files and remote modules. A null lookup can mean a genuinely absent record, but some interfaces cannot cleanly distinguish absence from every backend failure. Configure at least one stable local user/group sentinel and one stable remote user/group sentinel for every remote identity source that can own in-scope files. The supplied collector verifies each sentinel name-to-ID and ID-to-name before and after traversal. If a sentinel fails, a find root fails, or a candidate changes from unresolved to resolved during re-stat, the manifest is not complete and the detection rejects the batch. Sentinel success reduces but does not mathematically prove every NSS record is reachable; large cross-ID spikes still require identity-service triage before ownership changes.

## Step 1 — Approve one-filesystem scan roots and boundaries

Create a version-controlled root inventory with `host_class,scan_root,filesystem_type,device_id,identity_domain,owner,reason,enabled`. Use absolute canonical paths. Each configured root represents one filesystem traversal. GNU find's `-xdev` evaluates the root and entries on its `st_dev` but does not descend into directories on another device. Therefore `--root /` does not scan a separately mounted `/var`, `/home`, `/opt`, or application volume; add each approved mount as a separate root. Conversely, a bind mount backed by the same device can remain in scope because `-xdev` is not a general mount-point detector. Remove same-device bind aliases from the root tree or document the duplicate path behavior. The collector rejects overlapping configured roots on the same device and deduplicates an identical byte path across roots, but it intentionally does not merge distinct hard-link or alias paths merely because device/inode match.

Default to persistent local filesystems. Exclude `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, `/run`, container overlay/snapshot trees, removable media, network filesystems, backup mounts, offline images, and transient build trees unless a platform and identity owner explicitly defines their ownership semantics, scan node, performance window, and response. Because `find -P` is explicit, symbolic links are examined as links but never followed into their targets. Measure scan elapsed time, metadata I/O, storage latency, cache impact, process CPU, and application latency on a canary for each filesystem class. A daily low-traffic scan is a starting cadence, not a universal safe default. Never use a continuously running recursive search on latency-sensitive or remotely served storage without owner testing.

Record expected mounts independently. An event search cannot identify a filesystem that was unmounted before the collector started unless the collector's configured root fails or a separate mount-inventory comparison notices it. Require each configured path to exist and be a directory. Compare its current device and filesystem type with inventory before production rollout; extend the collector locally if strict type/device pinning is required. Treat a changed, missing, or unexpectedly merged mount as coverage drift rather than scanning the parent directory under the same pathname.

## Step 2 — Install and validate the complete-scan collector

Store the exact `scriptExample` as `/usr/local/libexec/collect_unowned_files.py`, root-owned, mode `0750`, not writable by application users or the forwarder. Record its hash. The script accepts repeated `--root`, `--nss-user NAME:UID`, and `--nss-group NAME:GID` arguments; sentinel arguments are mandatory. It runs absolute `/usr/bin/find` with argument-array execution, explicit `-P`, one starting root, `-xdev`, a parenthesized `(-nouser OR -nogroup)` expression, and `-print0`. Parentheses matter: the original unparenthesized `find / -nouser -o -nogroup` combines implicit actions and OR precedence in ways unsuitable for a transactional collector. NUL framing preserves spaces, newlines, glob characters, and leading dashes in names.

For each find candidate, the script calls `lstat` without following a symbolic link, records device/inode/type/mode/size/times and numeric IDs, and repeats user and group lookups. Exact raw path bytes are retained as base64; `path` is a display rendering and `path_hash` is SHA-256 over the original bytes. Exceptions key on the hash, not a lossy display path. If the file vanished after find, the script increments `vanished_path_count` and waits for the next scan. Other stat failures degrade the batch. If both IDs resolve on recheck, `resolution_changed_count` degrades the batch because the ownership answer changed during traversal. A nonzero find status degrades the scan root. Post-scan sentinel failure makes the entire manifest error/degraded. The final manifest is the transaction commit: findings without exactly one matching complete manifest are unusable.

Run the collector first against a disposable test filesystem. Confirm `root:0` user/group sentinels and selected remote sentinels resolve in both directions. Compare with the native interface by inspecting two finding events against `stat` output and `getent passwd <uid>` / `getent group <gid>`. Confirm device, inode, numeric mode, size, mtime, ctime, UID/GID, and resolution flags. Test a filename containing spaces, a newline, quotes, non-ASCII bytes, and a leading dash; verify base64 round-trip and stable path hash. Test a disappearing file and ensure only `vanished_path_count` changes. Test unreadable traversal, killed find, missing root, malformed sentinel, and NSS outage; none may create a complete manifest.

Schedule the collector as a separately privileged oneshot service, with one execution at a time, a bounded runtime longer than the measured p99 canary duration, and stdout appended to `/var/log/splunk/unowned-files.ndjson`. Use a root-owned service/timer or equivalent configuration-management primitive; preserve stderr/journal and process exit. Configure log rotation by rename/create with ownership retained and enough generations for forwarder outage recovery; avoid `copytruncate`, which can lose or duplicate concurrent lines. A killed process may leave findings without a manifest, which the SPL rejects; the collector-health search must alert on missing fresh manifests.

## Step 3 — Configure Splunk transport and field extraction

Create `TA_linux_unowned_files` rather than editing Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux. Grant the forwarder read-only access to the output directory/file. In `local/inputs.conf` use the deployment-selected index consistently:

```ini
[monitor:///var/log/splunk/unowned-files.ndjson]
disabled = 0
index = os
source = linux_unowned_files
sourcetype = linux:unowned_files
```

Configure event breaking and JSON extraction on the appropriate parsing/search tiers:

```ini
[linux:unowned_files]
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
LINE_BREAKER = ([\r\n]+)
TIME_PREFIX = "event_time"\s*:\s*"
TIME_FORMAT = %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ
MAX_TIMESTAMP_LOOKAHEAD = 20
TRUNCATE = 20000
KV_MODE = json
```

Keep one JSON object per physical line. Measure the longest escaped path event and set a reviewed `TRUNCATE` bound above it; 20,000 is only a starting value. Splunk documents `KV_MODE=json` as search-time extraction and warns against combining it with `INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS=JSON`, which duplicates fields. Inspect effective stanzas with `splunk btool inputs list --debug` on the forwarder and `splunk btool props list linux:unowned_files --debug` where parsing/search configuration applies. Confirm stable, unique Splunk `host` metadata; cloned host values can merge unrelated scan transactions.

For a scan ID, require exactly one manifest, observed finding-event count equal to `finding_count`, configured roots equal completed roots, zero failed roots/stat errors/resolution changes, and `collector_status=complete`. A clean scan legitimately contains only one zero-finding manifest. Build a separate source-health search from an expected-host inventory to compare latest manifest age, service exit, root counts, status, scan duration, find versions, error counters, and `_indextime-event_time`. Do not make the primary event search responsible for discovering hosts that emitted nothing.

## Step 4 — Create and understand the integrity-gated SPL

Save the top-level SPL as `linux_unowned_file_detection`. For a daily scan, schedule it after the scan's measured p99 duration plus forwarding delay; the supplied `earliest=-30h@h latest=-10m@m` is a completed-window starting point. Change lookback, latest delay, manifest freshness, timer, and exception tests together. The search first converts numeric fields, then finds the latest manifest start per host before filtering records. That ordering is essential: if the latest completed transaction has zero findings, an older finding must not remain active.

`eventstats` attaches manifest count, observed finding count, declared count, root completion, collector status, and error counters to every event in the same `host,scan_id`. Only finding records from exactly one complete, count-matched, all-roots-complete transaction survive. A duplicate/missing manifest, duplicate/truncated finding, failed root, stat error, unstable NSS answer, or malformed ownership field cannot produce a detection row. This fail-closed rule deliberately means collector failure is handled by the separate health alert rather than mixed with file findings.

The second predicate validates nonnegative numeric IDs, binary resolution flags, nonempty path/root, and a 64-character path hash. `issue_type` distinguishes user, group, and dual absence. User absence is high and group-only absence is medium as a routing default; severity does not prove exploitability. The exact exception lookup is applied only after batch integrity. Trigger when result count is greater than zero and group notifications by `host,issue_type,path_hash`; keep every scan result and scan ID. A changed issue type at the same path is a new condition and must not inherit another exception.

Create `linux_unowned_file_exceptions.csv` with the exact headers in `knownFalsePositives`, initially header-only. Define it in `transforms.conf`, restrict write access, version changes, and validate epochs and mandatory rationale through deployment tooling. An exception suppresses notification only; retain raw events and a governed exception-decision trail. Never add `uid`, `gid`, `directory-prefix`, `wildcard-host`, or permanent catch-all matching to the base lookup.

## Step 5 — Validate definition, mounts, transaction integrity, and controls

Execute the exact positive and negative `controlTest` scenarios in an isolated index and filesystem. Before creating the positive inode, prove the selected numeric IDs are absent through the same host NSS. Use numeric `chown` only on the disposable test mount and record the original state. Require exact event and result counts, IDs, issue type, severity, path hash, scan root, device/inode, and one complete manifest. Add user-only and group-only fixtures and verify `user_unowned`/high and `group_unowned`/medium respectively. Restore ownership or destroy the test filesystem when finished.

Test expression and traversal boundaries. A resolved file must not emit. A symbolic link must report its own ownership and must not cause target traversal. A different-device child mount must be skipped from its parent root and found when explicitly configured as a root. A same-device bind mount should demonstrate the documented `-xdev` limitation; resolve it through root policy rather than pretending the option blocks every mount. Test overlapping same-device root arguments and require collector rejection. Verify distinct hard-link paths remain distinct findings with shared device/inode.

Test NSS safety before any production alert. Disable or firewall the nonproduction directory-service path, expire a cache, stop the relevant NSS client daemon, and alter a sentinel mapping under identity-owner supervision. Require no complete manifest and a collector-health alert. Restore the service and require sentinels and ordinary remote IDs to resolve before accepting results. Test an ID deleted legitimately while NSS remains healthy and confirm it produces a file finding. This distinction is the central control objective.

Test event transaction failures: finding without manifest, manifest without finding when declared count is one, duplicate manifest, duplicate finding, wrong scan ID, two hosts sharing a scan ID, declared count above/below observed, root count mismatch, failed root, stat error, resolution change, status degraded/error, malformed numeric fields, bad hash length, stale manifest, and complete zero-finding scan after a prior positive scan. Only the valid latest complete transaction may produce rows. Activate and expire an exact exception at its lower/upper boundary; `valid_from_epoch` is inclusive and `valid_until_epoch` exclusive.

## Step 6 — Operationalize investigation, remediation, and evidence

Build the dashboard described in `visualization` with collector coverage adjacent to findings. Route account/identity context to the IAM/NSS owner and path/filesystem context to the platform or service owner. On a result, retrieve the exact manifest and raw event; confirm complete status, scan root, byte-path/base64, current `lstat`, `getent passwd <uid>`, `getent group <gid>`, sentinel health, mount/namespace context, package and restore history, file age, process/open-file use, ACLs/capabilities/labels, and application owner. A finding may disappear if an account is restored; preserve the original scan evidence and explain the transition.

Do not automatically run recursive `chown`, create an account matching an arbitrary number, delete the path, restart identity services, unmount storage, or quarantine a host from this alert. Numeric IDs can be valid in another namespace or source environment, and ownership changes can break package verification, service startup, backup restoration, access controls, and forensic provenance. Remediation requires an approved target owner/group, exact bounded path set, hard-link awareness, rollback or backup, service validation, and a post-change scan. If malicious activity is suspected, preserve inode/path metadata and file contents under incident-response procedures before mutation.

Review roots, NSS sentinels, exception inventory, collector versions, scan duration, and source-health coverage at least quarterly and after identity, mount, container, storage, OS, or application changes. Retain evidence under operational policy; the advisory 30-day field is not a compliance mandate. This documentation review leaves status draft until supported GNU find/glibc/Python/filesystem combinations, service privileges and overhead, JSON transport, SPL fixtures, NSS failure modes, and responder workflow have been tested and signed off.

## Step 7 — Troubleshoot source-specific failures

- **A large fleet-wide UID/GID spike appears:** stop remediation. Verify every local/remote sentinel, `getent` in both directions, `/etc/nsswitch.conf`, SSSD/LDAP/NIS/winbind health, DNS/TLS/network, and cache behavior. A complete manifest should not exist if configured sentinels failed; an incomplete sentinel set is a policy defect.
- **GNU find exits nonzero:** inspect bounded stderr and the service journal for permission denied, stale network handles, I/O errors, loops, or disappearing mount roots. Repair traversal or remove the filesystem from approved scope; do not redirect stderr to `/dev/null` or accept partial results.
- **A separate `/var` or `/home` has no findings:** `-xdev` prevented descent from `/`. Add the mount itself as an approved root and test identity/performance semantics. Do not remove `-xdev` from a fleet-wide root search.
- **A bind-mounted tree appears twice:** the bind may share `st_dev`, so `-xdev` cannot define that boundary. Remove the alias from the scanned tree/root policy or accept exact path-level visibility. Do not collapse all same-inode paths globally.
- **`resolution_changed_count` is nonzero:** NSS changed between find's predicate and collector recheck. Treat the scan as unstable; inspect identity backend/cache state and rerun only after sentinel and representative-ID stability.
- **`vanished_path_count` is nonzero:** active files disappeared between traversal and `lstat`. A small count on volatile but approved trees can be expected and does not create a finding; repeated/high counts justify moving the tree out of scope or changing cadence. Other stat errors remain batch-degrading.
- **Manifest count or declared/observed count mismatches:** inspect event breaking, truncation, file rotation, forwarder checkpoints, duplicate monitor stanzas, host identity, and scan IDs. Preserve the equality gate; never use `dedup` to conceal a broken transport transaction.
- **Paths are unreadable or oddly escaped:** use `path_b64` for exact bytes and `path_hash` for identity. Decode only in a controlled tool. Do not key exceptions on the display rendering.
- **A clean scan does not appear in the detection:** expected; a zero-finding scan has only a manifest. Verify it in collector-health coverage. The latest-manifest selection prevents old findings from persisting.
- **An unowned file on NFS/container overlay is missing:** those filesystems are excluded unless separately approved. Define their server/namespace identity semantics and scan location first; host NSS may be the wrong authority.
- **CIM or `tstats` cannot reproduce the search:** expected. Preserve raw custom events and transaction manifests because standard data models do not carry inode ownership plus NSS and complete-traversal integrity.
grandmaExplanation: We look for files whose owner number no longer matches a known person or group on that server. We first make sure the account directory and the scan itself are healthy, so an account-service outage is not mistaken for thousands of abandoned files.
hardware: Linux physical and virtual machines with qualified GNU find, Python/glibc NSS behavior, persistent local filesystems, and a separately privileged read-only traversal service. Network, removable, pseudo, transient container, offline-image, and unsupported namespace-owned filesystems remain outside scope until their identity and performance behavior is explicitly approved.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Emit GNU-find unowned-path findings plus one integrity manifest."""
import argparse
import base64
import datetime
import grp
import hashlib
import json
import os
import pwd
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import uuid

SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
FIND = "/usr/bin/find"


def utc(epoch):
    return datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(epoch, datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")


def emit(event):
    print(json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=True, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True), flush=True)


def display(raw):
    return raw.decode(sys.getfilesystemencoding(), errors="backslashreplace")


def parse_mapping(spec, kind):
    try:
        name, number = spec.rsplit(":", 1)
        value = int(number, 10)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid {kind} sentinel {spec!r}; expected NAME:ID")
    if not name or value < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid {kind} sentinel {spec!r}")
    return name, value


def check_sentinels(user_specs, group_specs):
    for spec in user_specs:
        name, uid = parse_mapping(spec, "user")
        if pwd.getpwnam(name).pw_uid != uid or pwd.getpwuid(uid).pw_uid != uid:
            raise RuntimeError(f"user NSS sentinel mismatch: {name}:{uid}")
    for spec in group_specs:
        name, gid = parse_mapping(spec, "group")
        if grp.getgrnam(name).gr_gid != gid or grp.getgrgid(gid).gr_gid != gid:
            raise RuntimeError(f"group NSS sentinel mismatch: {name}:{gid}")


def user_name(uid):
    try:
        return pwd.getpwuid(uid).pw_name
    except KeyError:
        return None


def group_name(gid):
    try:
        return grp.getgrgid(gid).gr_name
    except KeyError:
        return None


def file_type(mode):
    if stat.S_ISREG(mode):
        return "regular"
    if stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
        return "directory"
    if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
        return "symlink"
    if stat.S_ISCHR(mode):
        return "character_device"
    if stat.S_ISBLK(mode):
        return "block_device"
    if stat.S_ISFIFO(mode):
        return "fifo"
    if stat.S_ISSOCK(mode):
        return "socket"
    return "unknown"


def nul_records(stream):
    pending = b""
    while True:
        chunk = stream.read(65536)
        if not chunk:
            break
        pending += chunk
        fields = pending.split(b"\0")
        pending = fields.pop()
        for field in fields:
            if field:
                yield field
    if pending:
        raise RuntimeError("GNU find output ended without NUL framing")


def validated_roots(values):
    roots = []
    for value in values:
        if not os.path.isabs(value):
            raise ValueError(f"scan root must be absolute: {value!r}")
        root = os.path.realpath(value)
        details = os.stat(root, follow_symlinks=True)
        if not stat.S_ISDIR(details.st_mode):
            raise ValueError(f"scan root is not a directory: {root!r}")
        for previous, previous_dev in roots:
            nested = os.path.commonpath((previous, root)) in (previous, root)
            if nested and previous_dev == details.st_dev:
                raise ValueError(f"overlapping same-device roots: {previous!r}, {root!r}")
        roots.append((root, details.st_dev))
    if not roots:
        raise ValueError("at least one scan root is required")
    return roots


def find_version():
    result = subprocess.run([FIND, "--version"], capture_output=True, check=False, timeout=10)
    return result.stdout.decode("ascii", errors="replace").splitlines()[0][:160]


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--root", action="append", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--nss-user", action="append", required=True, help="required NAME:UID sentinel")
    parser.add_argument("--nss-group", action="append", required=True, help="required NAME:GID sentinel")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    started = int(time.time())
    scan_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    root_count = completed_roots = failed_roots = findings = 0
    vanished = stat_errors = resolution_changes = duplicate_paths = 0
    find_exits = []
    errors = []
    seen_paths = set()
    version = "unavailable"

    try:
        roots = validated_roots(args.root)
        root_count = len(roots)
        version = find_version()
        check_sentinels(args.nss_user, args.nss_group)

        for root, root_device in roots:
            root_raw = os.fsencode(root)
            command = [FIND, "-P", root, "-xdev", "(", "-nouser", "-o", "-nogroup", ")", "-print0"]
            with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as stderr_file:
                process = subprocess.Popen(command, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=stderr_file)
                try:
                    for path_raw in nul_records(process.stdout):
                        if path_raw in seen_paths:
                            duplicate_paths += 1
                            continue
                        seen_paths.add(path_raw)
                        try:
                            details = os.lstat(path_raw)
                        except FileNotFoundError:
                            vanished += 1
                            continue
                        except OSError:
                            stat_errors += 1
                            continue

                        resolved_user = user_name(details.st_uid)
                        resolved_group = group_name(details.st_gid)
                        unowned_user = int(resolved_user is None)
                        unowned_group = int(resolved_group is None)
                        if not (unowned_user or unowned_group):
                            resolution_changes += 1
                            continue

                        observed = int(time.time())
                        path_hash = hashlib.sha256(path_raw).hexdigest()
                        event = {
                            "event_time": utc(observed),
                            "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
                            "record_type": "ownership_finding",
                            "scan_id": scan_id,
                            "scan_started_epoch": started,
                            "scan_root": display(root_raw),
                            "scan_root_device_id": root_device,
                            "path": display(path_raw),
                            "path_b64": base64.b64encode(path_raw).decode("ascii"),
                            "path_hash": path_hash,
                            "device_id": details.st_dev,
                            "inode": details.st_ino,
                            "file_type": file_type(details.st_mode),
                            "mode_octal": format(stat.S_IMODE(details.st_mode), "04o"),
                            "size_bytes": details.st_size,
                            "mtime_epoch": int(details.st_mtime),
                            "ctime_epoch": int(details.st_ctime),
                            "uid": details.st_uid,
                            "gid": details.st_gid,
                            "is_unowned_user": unowned_user,
                            "is_unowned_group": unowned_group,
                            "user_name": resolved_user,
                            "group_name": resolved_group,
                        }
                        emit(event)
                        findings += 1
                finally:
                    if process.stdout:
                        process.stdout.close()
                exit_code = process.wait()
                stderr_file.seek(0)
                stderr_text = stderr_file.read(4096).decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip()
            find_exits.append(exit_code)
            if exit_code == 0:
                completed_roots += 1
            else:
                failed_roots += 1
                errors.append(f"find failed for {root!r} with exit {exit_code}: {stderr_text[:300]}")

        check_sentinels(args.nss_user, args.nss_group)
        if failed_roots or stat_errors or resolution_changes:
            status = "degraded"
        else:
            status = "complete"
    except Exception as exc:
        status = "error"
        errors.append(f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

    ended = int(time.time())
    manifest = {
        "event_time": utc(ended),
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "record_type": "manifest",
        "scan_id": scan_id,
        "scan_started_epoch": started,
        "scan_ended_epoch": ended,
        "scan_duration_seconds": ended - started,
        "collector_status": status,
        "collector_effective_uid": os.geteuid(),
        "find_version": version,
        "root_count": root_count,
        "completed_root_count": completed_roots,
        "failed_root_count": failed_roots,
        "finding_count": findings,
        "vanished_path_count": vanished,
        "stat_error_count": stat_errors,
        "resolution_changed_count": resolution_changes,
        "duplicate_path_count": duplicate_paths,
        "find_exit_codes": find_exits,
        "collector_error": " | ".join(errors)[:1000] if errors else None,
    }
    emit(manifest)
    return 0 if status == "complete" else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
